programme: LEF1 as the TCF/LEF Wnt-beta-catenin effector (CCND1, MYC, DKK4 among its targets) sits upstream of a RUNX-driven EMT switch: RUNX1 activates WNT2 to feed the same pathway and reprogram tumor-associated macrophages, RUNX2 drives an adenoma-to-carcinoma EMT programme, PCGF2 (Polycomb, MEL18) gates that switch by repressing ZEB1 and ZEB2 directly, and ETS1 executes the invasive output through MMP1, MMP7, SERPINE1 and TIMP1.
role_in_a: In colorectal cancer this is the canonical driver axis: Wnt/beta-catenin/LEF1 initiates tumorigenesis, RUNX2 pushes the adenoma-to-carcinoma transition and RUNX1 feeds back onto WNT2 while reprogramming macrophages, PCGF2 represses the EMT transcription factors it silences, and ETS1 supplies the matrix-remodeling output for invasion.
role_in_b: In head and neck squamous cell carcinoma the record here only documents LEF1: Wnt/beta-catenin signaling through LEF1-driven target genes is active in a subset of tumors, and disrupting CBP/beta-catenin attenuates this signaling and induces apoptosis. No head and neck evidence is retrieved for RUNX1, RUNX2, ETS1 or PCGF2 acting through this programme.
shared_axis: Both are epithelial/squamous carcinomas in which Wnt-LEF1 activity can license a RUNX-driven, Polycomb-gated EMT programme executed by ETS1-family invasion genes; if the same module operates in a Wnt-active head and neck subset as it does in colorectal tumors, it would explain the recurrence of this factor set across both diseases.
reasoning: The module is nameable and strongly placed in colorectal cancer, where LEF1, RUNX1, RUNX2, ETS1 and PCGF2 all have direct, disease-specific papers, so the CRC side of the axis is well anchored. The head and neck side rests on a single paper for LEF1 alone (31089983), with no retrieved evidence tying RUNX1, RUNX2, ETS1 or PCGF2 to head and neck cancer, so the cross-disease connection is carried more by the general fact that Wnt signaling operates in some HNSCC than by a documented shared module.
support: PMID 41258989 shows LEF1 suppressing ferroptosis via SLC7A11 in colorectal cancer; PMID 31089983 shows CBP/beta-catenin and porcupine inhibition attenuating Wnt signaling and inducing apoptosis in head and neck cancer cells, and explicitly concerns both LEF1 and head and neck cancer; PMID 42372471 and PMID 41985081 place RUNX1 in colorectal cancer, the latter showing RUNX1 activating WNT2 to reprogram tumor-associated macrophages; PMID 41511889 and PMID 42056097 place RUNX2 in colorectal EMT and adenoma-to-carcinoma transition; PMID 41912775 and PMID 41929510 place ETS1 in colorectal cancer progression and anti-tumor immunity; PMID 37598287 and PMID 33194594 place PCGF2 in colorectal cancer molecular subtyping; PMID 34398824 mentions PCGF2 in a head and neck ubiquitin-proteasome-system study but does not establish it acts through this programme there.
how_to_falsify: Take a Wnt-active head and neck squamous cell carcinoma line and a colorectal cancer line, knock down LEF1 in both, and check whether RUNX2, ETS1 target genes (MMP1/MMP7/MMP13) and PCGF2 targets (ZEB1/ZEB2) move concordantly in both lines; if the RUNX1/RUNX2/ETS1/PCGF2 targets fail to respond to LEF1 loss in the head and neck line while they do in the colorectal line, the shared module does not extend to head and neck cancer as proposed.
caveats: Evidence comes from 874 patient-group comparisons across only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance fractions (227-236 out of 874, roughly 26-27%) are modest and similar across all listed factors rather than pointing to one dominant driver. The single-view exclusions (STAT2, FOXP4, CDX4, THAP1, ETV3, PHF8, SALL4, CEBPA, TLE5, HOXB13, ZNF503, ZNF304) show this account is not built on one subgroup's idiosyncratic top hit. PHF5A, ZNF354C, EWSR1, SSRP1, PRDM2, KAT5 and PLAGL1 were left out of the carrying set because their retrieved literature is off-topic, pan-cancer, or absent for head and neck cancer, not because they were tissue-generic exclusions.
